steps.title: Interactive: Room-by-Room Safety Checklist
steps.content:
Use this checklist during every visit to reduce falls and injuries.

LIVING AREAS
- Clear clutter and secure cords along walls.
- Remove or tape down loose rugs.
- Ensure lamps and light switches are easy to reach.
- Keep frequently used items within reach.

BATHROOM
- Check that grab bars are sturdy.
- Use non-slip mats in tub and on floor.
- Set water heater below 120°F to avoid burns.
- Never rush a client who needs help toileting or bathing.

BEDROOM
- Keep a nightlight on.
- Place a lamp and phone within reach of the bed.
- Ensure the path from bed to bathroom is clear.

KITCHEN
- Clean spills immediately.
- Keep heavy items at waist level.
- Never leave cooking unattended.
- Check that smoke detectors work.

OUTDOORS / ENTRY
- Remove leaves, ice, or objects from walkways.
- Ensure handrails are secure.
- Lock doors and set alarms per the care plan.

steps.title: Body Mechanics & Safe Lifting
steps.content:
PROTECTING YOUR BACK
Caregiving often requires bending, lifting, and assisting with movement. Using proper body mechanics protects you and the client from injury.

LIFTING RULES
- Plan the lift before you begin.
- Keep your feet shoulder-width apart for a stable base.
- Bend your knees and keep your back straight.
- Lift with your leg muscles, not your back.
- Hold the load close to your body.
- Avoid twisting; turn your whole body.
- Do not reach or jerk.

TRANSFERS
- Explain each step to the client.
- Use a gait or transfer belt when available and you are trained.
- Lock wheelchair brakes before standing transfers.
- Never pull a client up by the arms or wrists.
- Ask for help when a client needs more support than you can safely provide.

WHEN TO STOP
If a client is too heavy, uncooperative, or the surface is unsafe, stop and call the office for assistance. Your safety matters too.
